A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, we have successfully developed a multi-robot learning based task-planning technique, which is able to plan the task of transporting objects from source to destination, in a multi-robot environment, with the help of a single Q-table.

we have developed a novel multi-agent Q-learning algorithm, which improves speed of convergence by introducing two novel properties, namely exploration of the team goal and selection of the joint action, and by offering appropriate rewards to the agents.

the extended multi-agent Q-learning algorithm with exploration of team-goal and intersection of individual preferred actions outperforms its classical multi-agent Qlearning counterpart with respect to speed of learning, while the proposed strategy of rewarding exploration of the teamgoal and individual goals yields significant improvement in performance of multi-agent planning.

we have proposed two extensions to the traditional multi-agent Qlearning algorithm to improve the speed of convergence.

the proposed algorithms can be used to plan the cooperative task in the case where the agents are capable of reaching their individual goal states but are unable to reach their individual goals simultaneously.
the speed of convergence can be improved by incorporating exploration of the team goal and by selecting the joint action at a joint state.
